propositions: The reconciler's cursor advances to newest event time unconditionally, permanently dropping candidates that failed to vote in the first pass where they appeared, because the events-log ?t1= filter is server-side inclusive.

A patch-set upload event delivered by the webhook is lost at-most-once by design (Gerrit plugin discards after maxTries; async queue is volatile), leaving the change vote-less and unreachable to future reconciler passes.
The reconciler was contracted to re-drive abandoned candidates automatically on the next pass, but the guarding test ignored the since parameter, masking the defect through false green.

Two distinct manual nudges (recheck-review comment and no-op rebase) revive stalled changes by minting new events-log entries with timestamps after the cursor, confirming the root cause is event-based rather than state-based.
The queue depth, held_back candidates, and chronically-failing holdback state are not observable today, leaving agents unable to distinguish dropped events from slow queues or bot downtime.
